## The big idea

::: {.kicker}
Onboarding an SDR today
:::

::: {.lead}
A new Sales Development Rep takes **12 weeks** to ramp — and today that ramp is slow, inconsistent, and barely measured.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="statgrid warn">
  <div class="stat"><span class="num">42%</span><span class="lab">hit quota</span><span class="sub">new SDRs (RepVue, Feb 2026)</span></div>
  <div class="stat"><span class="num">24–72h</span><span class="lab">coaching feedback lag</span><span class="sub">on cold-call reviews</span></div>
  <div class="stat"><span class="num">3–5h</span><span class="lab">manual call review</span><span class="sub">per manager, per week</span></div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-card .filled}
**Our redesign — one AI coworker for the whole journey:** draft the plan → coach the calls → certify at week 12 → debrief to improve the program. A **Manager** reviews every consequential step.
:::

## The redesigned workflow

::: {.lead}
Four phases — pre-boarding, ramp, certification, post-cert debrief — with a Manager review gate in each.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="workflow">
  <div class="wf-phase">

    <div class="wf-step auto"><span class="t">Welcome email</span><span class="s">template slot-fill</span></div>
```

## Under the hood

::: {.lead}
Every request — a hire, a question, a transcript — flows through the same pipeline.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="arch">
  <div class="arch-step"><span class="t">Input</span><span class="s">hire · question · transcript</span></div>
  <div class="arch-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="arch-step"><span class="t">Skills + automations</span><span class="s">7 LLM skills · 2 deterministic</span></div>
  <div class="arch-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="arch-step"><span class="t">RAG retrieval</span><span class="s">BM25 + ChromaDB · 16 docs</span></div>
  <div class="arch-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="arch-step accent"><span class="t">JSON envelope</span><span class="s">confidence · sources · review flag</span></div>
  <div class="arch-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="arch-step"><span class="t">React UI</span><span class="s">9 screens · Manager / SDR</span></div>
  <div class="arch-arrow">→</div>
  <div class="arch-step"><span class="t">Human gate</span><span class="s">logged to decision_log.json</span></div>
</div>
<div class="techstrip">
  <span><b>7</b> LLM skills</span><span><b>2</b> automations</span><span><b>2</b> retrievers</span><span><b>2</b> MCP servers</span><span><b>9</b> UI screens</span><span><b>153</b> tests passing</span>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-card}
One uniform envelope between every step makes the workflow **auditable, idempotent, and safe to gate**.
:::

## Data, evidence & AI usage

::: {.kicker}
What the AI uses — and what the user can inspect
:::

```{=html}
<div class="cards two">
  <div class="card"><span class="h">Data it uses</span>SDR &amp; AE profiles · per-hire summaries · simulation personas · a 7-SDR records set · call transcripts pasted by the user.</div>
  <div class="card"><span class="h">Documents (RAG)</span>A <b>16-doc</b> internal knowledge base — onboarding policy, quota ramp, objection handbook, cold-call rubric, territory + vertical playbooks, certification rubric &amp; exam — plus 7 public references.</div>
  <div class="card green"><span class="h">Tools / functions</span><b>7</b> LLM skills · <b>2</b> deterministic automations · <b>2</b> retrievers (BM25 + ChromaDB) · <b>2</b> MCP servers.</div>
  <div class="card"><span class="h">Evidence the user sees</span>An <b>EvidencePanel</b> with numbered cited sources + match scores · inline <code>[n]</code> citations that open the exact passage · per-dimension cards quoting the SDR's own work verbatim.</div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-card .amber}
**When evidence is weak or missing:** the tutor cites a source or refuses (no bluffing) · confidence &lt; 0.60 blocks auto-complete and pauses for review · a server-side recompute overrides the AI's certification verdict if they disagree.
:::

## Human stays in control — five gates

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="54%"}

```{=html}
<div class="gates">
  <div class="gate"><span class="n">1</span><span><b>Pre-boarding plan</b> — Manager approves / edits / rejects / escalates</span></div>
  <div class="gate"><span class="n">2</span><span><b>AI Tutor answer</b> — SDR approves / rejects; rejection re-enters retrieval</span></div>
  <div class="gate"><span class="n">3</span><span><b>Coaching note</b> — Manager reviews before the SDR sees it</span></div>
  <div class="gate"><span class="n">4</span><span><b>Certification</b> — Manager decides Pass/Fail with a required comment</span></div>
  <div class="gate"><span class="n">5</span><span><b>Onboarding debrief</b> — Manager reviews, then shares with enablement</span></div>
</div>
```

:::
::: {.column width="46%"}

```{=html}
<div class="cards">
  <div class="card amber"><span class="h">Two hard safeguards</span>Confidence &lt; 0.60 <b>blocks auto-complete</b> and pauses for review · a server-side recompute <b>overrides</b> the AI's certification verdict if they disagree.</div>
  <div class="card"><span class="h">Every decision logged</span>Approve / edit / reject / escalate is written to <code>decision_log.json</code> with feature, action and timestamp — a full audit trail.</div>
</div>
```

:::
:::

## Testing — the kinds of checks we ran

::: {.lead}
We didn't just ship the AI Tutor — an automated **DeepEval** suite judges its answers, rerun to trust the trend over noise.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="cards two">
  <div class="card"><span class="h">10 cases × 4 checks</span><b>Faithfulness</b> — stays within retrieved sources? · <b>Answer relevancy</b> — answers what was asked? · <b>Citation + next-step</b> — cites <code>[n]</code> and a concrete action? · <b>SDR face-validity</b> — useful to a real SDR? Cases span everyday, edge (vague / no-source), and predicted-failure inputs.</div>
  <div class="card green"><span class="h">What it caught — and the fix</span>It flagged real failures: over-answering vague questions, a fabricated module-ID, generic next-steps. We changed <b>one thing</b> (narrow broad questions + block ungrounded identifiers), reran 6× — the weak case went from failing to passing and fabrication disappeared.</div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-card .amber}
**Honest:** one rule over-formalized a couple of answers, and the biggest remaining gap is **knowledge-base coverage** — a content fix, not a prompt fix.
:::

## Face validity — would a sales leader believe this?

```{=html}
<div class="cards two">
  <div class="card"><span class="h">The size is believable</span>The AI only compresses what it's genuinely good at — drafting plans, retrieving answers, scoring calls. The Manager's review time is <b>added back in</b>, so the headline cuts are net savings, not magic.</div>
  <div class="card"><span class="h">The direction is right</span>Every consequential decision still needs a human: the Manager approves plans and coaching notes, and the certification AI is <b>advisory</b> — the Manager makes the Pass/Fail call.</div>
  <div class="card green"><span class="h">It's grounded, not guessed</span>Tutor answers cite the source passage behind each claim (Faithfulness ~8.7/10 across our runs). When the AI isn't sure, it <b>flags for review</b> instead of bluffing.</div>
  <div class="card amber"><span class="h">Where we're honest</span>Certification is demoed on a synthetic 7-SDR cohort, and the recurring coaching saving assumes a typical weekly call volume — both clearly labeled as assumptions.</div>
</div>
```
